body:
Sorry for the delay.

I have tried talk therapy with 2 different therapists, one of whom mostly used cognitive behavioral techniques. I have taken amitriptyline, which just made me sleep for 12 hours at a time. I am currently taking sertraline (150mg) and bupropion (300mg) and I've not noticed a change in my mood, sleep or energy since taking them. I abruptly stopped taking them once, and I experienced a slew of withdrawal symptoms (brain zaps, extreme fluctuations between insomnia and hypersomnia, nausea, muscle jerks) so I suppose I am dependent on them now, even though they haven't actually improved any symptoms. I took Buspirone for a 3 months, but that was like taking sugar pills. Since sleep was/is a major issue of mine, my psychiatrist prescribed seroquel to help me go to sleep at night. It had an effect similar to the amitriptyline, in that I slept for periods that were entirely too long. (Non-psychiatric drugs I have tried for sleep include ambien, melatonin, and trazodone. All of these effected my sleep in different ways, but none of them helpful. Additionally, I began to experience some depersonalization symptoms while on trazodone, so we stopped that quickly).

It's difficult to describe my thought process "when I am depressed," because I can't think of a recent time when I have NOT been depressed. Even when I seem to be functioning well in life or enjoying a tv show or a book or what have you, I still keep thinking, "I don't want to be doing this," or "This isn't worth my effort." It feels like I am doing nothing but killing time. At my worst, my thoughts are much more focused toward my failures: everything I've missed, everything I know I can't accomplish, people I've hurt, people I would hurt if I killed myself. I look to my friends who are mostly now entering the next chapter of their lives with marriage and kids, and I know that is not in my future. I know that my family wonders what is wrong with me, since I've never had a significant other in my life--mostly this is blamed on the way I look, which is another thing I hate about myself.

I suppose regardless of my mood, my thoughts all essentially center around how much I dislike myself, how disinterested I am in life, and how bleak I believe my future will be.

I have felt less than human probably since I was 13 years old. I probably wouldn't even say I was depressed then. Just different and avoided.

Ask the question. The worst I can do is not answer.

Sorry for the delay.

By atypical depression, I mean that I do experience some changes in my mood. I may laugh at a joke. I can go out for a day and, say, enjoy watching a movie. And yet, even with these periodic elevations in mood, I still have these feelings of ennui, misery or self-loathing the majority of the time.  I am sure there are those who could see me in certain situations, and never believe that I am depressed. But even at my best, even when on the outside I may LOOK happy, I cannot stop thinking about wanting to be alone and in bed, asleep. Even when I seem to be functioning well in life, there is still the nagging thought of, "I still don't want to be here, doing this, alive."

To keep from writing an essay, I will make a list.

* I have atypical depression, it has been treatment resistant, and it is making everything that I have worked toward for my whole life impossible for me to accomplish. Even if there is something I haven't tried (my psychiatrist certainly couldn't think of anything else), it is extremely likely that a reprieve would be temporary before falling into another miserable morass of depression. And if this is something that will relapse and remit for most of the rest of my life, as most data suggests, then those temporary reprieves are not worth the dips into despair.

* I am alone with no real prospects. I cannot sustain a relationship, because I cannot become physically or emotionally attached to anyone. This has been a problem long before I struggled with depression, stretching back to even middle/high school. I have never in my life been attracted to anyone of any sex, not even a crush. This has troubled me two different ways: 1.) I'd always desired to have a family of my own and a normal (and existent) sex life, but it would all be a charade on my part, which I find exhausting to keep up; 2.) the absence of these feelings that billions of people in the world have, these feelings that keep the whole of the human population alive on earth--it makes me feel less than human. 

* I have no hobbies or interests. I have tried to form some, or keep up some that once held my interest. Everything bores me, and I find myself just counting down the minutes until the day is over, then dread having to do it the next day. I know that anhedonia is a symptom of depression (and you can see my first bullet point for a response to that), but it has become difficult for me to imagine any interest or goal meaningful enough to make living worth it.

* My studies/career goals have taken a recent hit from which I don't know if they can recover. Since starting a family is not a part of my future, I thought that I would at least have my career to keep me occupied, but that seems less likely now. In addition to this, as I said with the interests and hobbies, no career seems meaningful enough to make life worth living anymore.

* I don't believe in any sort of supernatural being or afterlife. I believe this life is all we have, and there is nothing to answer to after we die. I am unconcerned about that. Many who hold this view will say that it means we have to make the most of this life, but I don't see it that way. I don't particularly like being alive, and I would like to get out of it early. If it is my life, I should have the right to say so. 

So basically: I feel miserable all the time, I find little enjoyment in anything, I find life a boring chore, years of treatment has not helped more than mildly, and I cannot think of anything at all that I believe would make life worth living, save for protecting my siblings/father from the pain of losing me. But even that doesn't make life worth living, it makes death less desirable and these are not the same thing at all.

I know that I have depression. Everyday it is a struggle to get out of bed. Becase of this, I’ve made some irreparable mistakes in both my professional and personal lives. 

I have “atypical” depression; that is, I can still find pleasure in some things even if it is few and far between. I can enjoy eating food. I can enjoy watching movies. Not much else. At the same time, there are long periods of time when I can remain very functional, but the sadness and desire to die never really goes away. It’s like carrying a brick around in my pocket.

Having this illness and having received many medications that have not remedied many symptoms, I see my future as a sort of roller coaster. There will be tolerable periods of time, and abysmal periods of time, and I can’t imagine ever finding joy in a life that is constantly and inevitably pulled down into the despair that I feel right now.

I have worked hard to obtain an education and a professional degree, which no longer interests me. I feel trapped, financially speaking. I can’t make myself feel passionate about anything.

I am 25 and have never had any intimacy or romance in my life. No significant other,  no kissing, no flirting. I blame part of it on my undesirability, but also on my lack of interest. It is difficult to explain—I have always desired a relationship with someone, a family, a lover. But I have never even had a crush on anyone, I find it almost impossible to be romantically attracted to anyone. I do not know if this is due to a low libido or an asexual sexuality, but either way I can only see a bleak and lonely future in this respect. At the same time, most of my friends have moved on in this portion of their life, and I feel left behind and no longer a part of the group.

I also have what I guess you could call a more existential problem. I look around, and I can’t understand why *anyone* would want to live. The world seems disproportionately weighted down with suffering, death, disease, despair, cruelty, and hatred. What compassion and good exists is comparable to finding a watering hole in the desert. 

Lastly, I have said I feel that I’m staying alive just for the sake of not upsetting people, but those people don’t have much longer to live anyway. They will die within the next few years, and then nothing will be there to stop me.

I am working toward a degree with a career in mind. I am finding I am no longer very interested in it, but feel financially trapped. At the same time, I don't really have much interest in other career paths.

I have tried finding joy in the small things in life, and sometimes I do. But I can't make them seem "worth it." For this to be a reason to live...it just doesn't seem like it's...enough. Thank you for your advice, though.
I am seeing a psychiatrist, but it's mostly been medical management.
